summary: Friday's AI and chip-led selloff sent the S&P 500 into a correction and the Nasdaq to its worst week since 2020, while Fed hike odds near 99% kept the dollar strong and gold weak. Tokyo is closed today, so Asia trades thin.
events_next_24h: Mon all day JPY Japan market holiday (Labor Thanksgiving Day), thin liquidity
Forex Factory feed unavailable this run: check it for other high-impact items
tier1_next_14d: US PCE (Oct) + Q3 GDP 2nd estimate · Thu 26 Nov 12:30am

ES.why: Friday's AI/chip rout sank the S&P 3.7% into a correction with 99% odds of a Fed hike; funds are crowded long (94th pct), so more longs may unwind.
ES.risk: A sharp oversold bounce after a 7-day losing streak, or softer Fed talk.

NQ.why: Nasdaq fell 5.3% Friday (worst week since 2020) as semis lost 10.7% and Nvidia 13.8%; funds still lean long (85th pct), leaving room to sell.
NQ.risk: A relief rally in chips or a calming Nvidia headline could spark a squeeze.

YM.why: The Dow fell less (-1.9%) than tech but still slid with the broad risk-off and Fed hike pricing.
YM.risk: Rotation out of tech into value names could hold the Dow up.

RTY.why: Rate-hike pricing hurts small caps, but I couldn't confirm Friday's Russell close or positioning, so no call.
RTY.risk: A clear Russell move with the broad tape would set the direction.

NKD.why: Nikkei fell over 5% Friday on the chip rout and CME NKD follows NQ while Tokyo is shut today; funds are neutral (32nd pct).
NKD.risk: A US futures bounce in thin holiday trade, or a weaker yen.

6J.why: Strong dollar and Fed hikes push the yen weaker, but USD/JPY sits near 160 where Japan has intervened and a BoJ Dec hike is ~86% expected.
6J.risk: A break above 160 with no intervention (bearish yen) or MoF action (bullish yen).

6E.why: The dollar is near a 19-month high on Fed hike bets, but I found no fresh euro-specific driver overnight.
6E.risk: A big dollar move on Fed talk or US data.

6B.why: Dollar strength weighs on sterling, but I couldn't verify Friday's GBP close or a UK-specific catalyst.
6B.risk: Confirmed new 2026 lows in GBP/USD would tilt it bearish.

6A.why: The Aussie is a risk-sensitive currency and global stocks are in a rout while the Fed is set to hike.
6A.risk: A rebound in global stocks or China-led risk appetite.

ZN.why: Treasuries rallied as a safe haven Friday, pushing the 10-year yield down to 4.93% from 5.04%, though Fed hike pricing caps gains.
ZN.risk: Hawkish Fed speakers or a stock rebound pulling money out of bonds.

GC.why: Gold dropped about 8% last week, near 14-month lows, on a strong dollar and Fed hike bets; funds lean short (20th pct), so a snap-back is possible.
GC.risk: A dollar reversal or haven buying if the stock rout deepens.

CL.why: Brent rose 0.6% to $92.57 Friday on Hormuz tension in the US-Iran war, and funds are crowded short (10th pct), a squeeze risk.
CL.risk: Fresh surplus forecasts or demand fears from the risk-off selloff.
